claim: Let \(H\) be any simple graph on \(n\ge1\) vertices and let \(D=\overline{K_2}\vee H\) be its double cone, with conical vertices \(a,b\). For the continuous-time quantum walk generated by the combinatorial Laplacian, the apex-to-apex amplitude is independent of the edges of \(H\): \[A_n(t)=\langle b|e^{-itL(D)}|a\rangle=\frac1{n+2}+\frac{n}{2(n+2)}e^{-i(n+2)t}-\frac12e^{-int}.\] The exact all-time optimal transfer fidelity is \[\max_{t\in\mathbb R}|A_n(t)|^2=\begin{cases}\cos^2\!\bigl(\frac{\pi}{2(n+2)}\bigr),&n\text{ odd},\\\cos^2\!\bigl(\frac{\pi}{n+2}\bigr),&n\equiv0\pmod4,\\1,&n\equiv2\pmod4.\end{cases}\] Hence the known perfect-transfer condition \(n\equiv2\pmod4\) is quantitatively sharp: in the two non-perfect congruence classes the best possible infidelity is respectively \(\sin^2(\pi/[2(n+2)])\) and \(\sin^2(\pi/(n+2))\), both of order \(n^{-2}\), and no choice of the internal graph \(H\) can improve it.

integrity.computational_dependence: none for the proof; finite numerical replay is supplementary
integrity.novelty_scope: Sharp all-time optimization of the known double-cone amplitude only.

scientific_limitations: Only simple unweighted double cones and the combinatorial Laplacian are covered.
The join-amplitude identity and the congruence criterion for perfect transfer are prior work.
Originality is restricted to the exact global fidelity optimum and its non-perfect deficit formulas.
Because the optimization is elementary after the prior amplitude identity, an equivalent formula may exist in unindexed literature.
title: Exact optimal apex-transfer fidelity for every Laplacian double cone
